name: Shackleton Crater Rim
notes: Connecting Ridge near Shackleton crater rim. Peaks of quasi-eternal light with grazing solar illumination.
psrDetails: Overlooks Shackleton interior PSR (<40 K volatile cold trap)

name: Malapert Massif
notes: Highland plateau massif (+5,000 m) offering broad, uninterrupted Earth direct-to-Earth line-of-sight.
psrDetails: Elevated highland plateau massif; ~18 km from cold traps

name: Haworth Crater Rim
notes: High crater rim adjacent to deep sub-40K cold trap containing volatile water ice deposits.
psrDetails: Directly borders Haworth crater interior PSR cold traps

name: Intuitive Machines IM-1 (Odysseus)
notes: First commercial CLPS soft landing near Malapert A crater at high southern latitude (Feb 2024).
psrDetails: Malapert A apron; elevated outside primary permanent shadows

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti Point)
notes: Historic high-latitude southern landing site near Manzinus C crater.
psrDetails: High-latitude southern plain; no permanent shadow (diurnal sun)

name: Nobile Crater Region
notes: Mountainous highland plateau bordering Nobile crater selected for volatile rover exploration.
psrDetails: VIPER exploration ridge bordering Nobile micro-cold-traps

name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
notes: Equatorial baseline site demonstrating standard 14-day lunar day and 14-day lunar night cycle.
psrDetails: Equatorial mare basalt plain; standard 14-day diurnal cycle

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow)
notes: Deep lunar valley surrounded by North and South Massifs; last human surface mission of Apollo.
psrDetails: Taurus-Littrow valley floor surrounded by steep massifs

name: de Gerlache Rim
notes: High sunlit ridge crest between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters.
psrDetails: Connecting ridge spine between Shackleton and de Gerlache PSRs

name: Amundsen Crater Rim
notes: Major 105km South polar impact crater with illuminated rim summits.
psrDetails: Illuminated rim crest bordering deep Amundsen floor PSR

name: Faustini Crater Rim
notes: Perpetually shadowed crater basin bounded by sunlit highlands.
psrDetails: Perpetually shadowed crater basin bounded by sunlit highlands

name: Apollo 12 (Ocean of Storms)
notes: Pinpoint precision landing adjacent to the Surveyor 3 robotic probe.
psrDetails: Equatorial Oceanus Procellarum; standard diurnal cycle

name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
notes: Fra Mauro highlands exploration and Cone crater rim geological survey.
psrDetails: Fra Mauro highland ridge and Cone crater slope

name: Apollo 15 (Hadley Rille)
notes: First mission deploying the Lunar Roving Vehicle alongside the deep Hadley canyon.
psrDetails: Hadley Rille basalt plain and Apennine front

name: Apollo 16 (Descartes Highlands)
notes: Highland plateau sampling of the ancient Cayley formation and Descartes volcanic range.
psrDetails: Descartes highland plateau; standard diurnal cycle

name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán / Far Side)
notes: First ever soft landing on the lunar far side inside South Pole-Aitken basin.
psrDetails: Von Karman crater floor on lunar far side

name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo Basin / Far Side)
notes: First successful robotic sample return mission from the lunar far side.
psrDetails: Apollo basin plain on lunar far side

name: Tycho Crater
notes: Prominent 85km impact crater with brilliant ray system extending across 1,500km.
psrDetails: Central peak and terraced walls; high relief

name: Copernicus Crater
notes: Classic 93km impact crater with terraced walls and 1.2km central peak complex.
psrDetails: Central peak and impact terraces; steep rim

name: Mare Tranquillitatis
notes: Broad basaltic mare plain formed by ancient flood basalt eruptions.
psrDetails: Smooth volcanic flood basalt mare plain

name: Oceanus Procellarum
notes: The largest lunar mare, spanning over 2,500km across the western near side.
psrDetails: Extensive basalt plain with low relief

name: Lunar North Pole
notes: Lunar geographic North Pole surrounded by deep craters Peary, Hermite, and Byrd.
psrDetails: Surrounded by deep craters Peary, Hermite, and Byrd

name: Lunar South Pole
notes: Lunar geographic South Pole situated directly on the rim crest of Shackleton crater.
psrDetails: True South Pole on Shackleton rim flank above deep cryogenic shadow
